title: Introduction to Website Design
description: This course teaches proper website design techniques to students from all degree programs. Topics include visual design and graphics, information architecture, usability and accessibility, communication, adaptation to audience, markup languages, and development tools and processes. Coursework is focused on applying website design principles and techniques to projects in the students' disciplines. The course is gauged for beginners who are computer competent; it does not teach computer programming.

title: Problem Solving with Object-Oriented Programming
description: The ability to solve problems creatively using computational methods has become important to professionals in many disciplines. This interdisciplinary course is designed for students who are not necessarily intent on becoming computer programmers but are interested in understanding the principles that govern Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) and software development in order to assist with problem-solving in their own disciplines. The course addresses a variety of topics including algorithm building principles, problem-solving strategies, how to analyze problems to identify requirements, and how to design an object-oriented solution. Students design, write, and debug computer programs.

title: Innovation & Emerging Technologies
description: Students work with emerging tech that encourages critical thinking, interdisciplinary perspectives, and lifelong learning skills. It introduces students to tools and techniques used to design, develop, and evaluate innovative technologies, guides students through the development of their own innovations, and offers students a perspective on tech innovation through a wide variety of emerging techs.

title: Information Ethics for the 21st Century
description: Identify current information ethics challenges; gain the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to make informed ethical decisions in the digital age, through observation, practice, comparison, reading, and analyzing the literature about information ethics.

title: Empowering Health Consumers in the eHealth Era
description: This course explores the use of emerging technologies for health education, disease prevention, and chronic disease management. Students will use patient-centered and research-based approaches to assess users' health and information needs in order to design effective eHealth solutions.

title: Information Literacy & Society
description: This course introduces students to the concepts of information literacy and what it means to be information literate in 21st century society. Students will address persistent questions associated with information literacy by learning searching skills, gathering information from primary and derivative sources, and conducting information quality analyses.

title: The Unintended Consequences of Information Technology
description: This course explores the societal implications and unintended consequences of information technology. It provides students the opportunity to explore how society's increased reliance on information technology has changed the way we interact with each other and the world around us.

title: Web Applications Development
description: This course introduces students to industry best practices and standards in proper website design and development, using object-oriented programming techniques. Topics include visual design and graphics, information architecture, usability and accessibility, communication, adaptation to audience, markup languages, and development tools and processes. The course provides a solid foundation in computer programming for the web: syntax and data structures, conditionals, objects, scope, the DOM and event handling.

title: Digital Storytelling in Information Environments
description: Digital storytelling uses virtual spaces and digital technologies to support human oral storytelling. This course helps students build their presentation skills through an understanding of the role of storytelling in the context of information environments such as the family, library, school, business, and social media.

title: Database Concepts
description: This course examines relational database management systems using a typical, commercial DBMS. Topics include data modeling, database design, implementation, forms and reports, and remote access to databases. The goal of this course is to provide students with a basic understanding of database design, implementation, and management concepts and techniques.

title: Technical Communication for the Information Professions
description: The ability to communicate about technical or specialized topics to various audiences is critical to making information usable and accessible and is an important skill for all information professionals to have. This course emphasizes the principles of clear and effective written and oral communication as applied in information technology fields.

title: Research and Data Analysis in Information Technology
description: This course provides students with an understanding of methods and tools used by information professionals for research and data analysis. It focuses on both quantitative and qualitative methods in information technology professions including surveys, interviews, need assessments, requirements analysis, and transaction log analysis.

title: Information Technologies
description: This course provides a solid foundation in the fundamental concepts, theories and principles in information technology and discusses critical issues surrounding their use and how they impact everyday life. An understanding of the concepts and principles underlying the design and use of digital devices, computer hardware, software, telecommunications, networking and multimedia is an integral part of any IT curriculum.

title: Information Systems and Services
description: This course provides an overview of information systems concepts and practice including system management, maintenance, assurance, and reporting services, physical and human resources. It includes an introduction to information system hardware components, operating systems, scripting languages, with practical training in databases and networked servers.

title: Cybersecurity for Digital Citizenship
description: This course provides a series of up-to-date topical lectures and discussions on state-of-the-art cybersecurity that will orient the digital citizen for the future. The course prepares students to understand the most common cyber-threat types, hacking techniques and fundamental protection strategies.

title: Advanced Database Management
description: This course explores various topics in database management systems (DBMS), using a typical commercial DMBS (e.g., MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle). Administration, security, stored procedures, triggers, transactions, functions, data mining, data warehousing, and remote access to databases are some of the topics covered.

title: Intermediate Database Management
description: Database analysis transcends a wide range of skills from basic modeling analysis to understanding users, what they do, as well as statistical analysis and data-mining. This course examines relational database management systems using a typical, commercial DBMS, such as Microsoft Access and/or MySQL and Oracle.

title: Information Architecture
description: This course provides an introduction to the scope and methods of information architecture, including project strategy; project scope; audience research; organization schemes, categories, and labels; identifying functional and content requirements; and interface design.

title: Writing for the Information Professions
description: Offers practical hands-on experience with forms and practices of technical and professional writing, including documentation, correspondence, audience analysis, writing for social media, evaluation, and review.

title: Advanced Mobile Applications Development
description: This concepts- and projects-oriented course examines advanced techniques of mobile application design and development. Course applications will utilize and integrate specific mobile device features involving interface design and testing, with a priority on data handling and validation methods, life cycle events, local and remote process services, location based facilities, device sensors, network and web application programming interfaces (APIs).

title: User Experience Design
description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the user experience design process, and is intended to familiarize students with the methods, concepts, and techniques necessary to make user experience design an integral part of developing information interfaces.

title: Advanced Web Applications Development
description: This course provides a foundation in developing web applications with an emphasis on server-side concepts, tools and methods. Topics include basic web application programming, advanced object-oriented programming (OOP) and web application development.

title: Extensible Enterprise Solutions
description: Application design and development are much needed skills in current professional job markets. Procedural programming, as well as object-oriented programming (OOP), are widely accepted and used methodologies for designing modern systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications
description: This course is an explorative introduction into artificial intelligence. AI and its related fields are used in many areas: business and health analytics, security, energy production, image and biometric analysis and recognition, weather forecasting.

title: Social Media Management
description: This course explores the tools and techniques of professional social media management through hands-on work with designing and managing social media campaigns. Students participating in this class will actively design, implement, and coordinate a series of social media management tasks.

title: Mobile Web Application Development
description: This course focuses on concepts and best practices for developing and managing 'mobile-first' technology projects. It covers processes and requirements for developing mobile web applications and principles for effective interface and user experience design.

title: Information Technology Leadership
description: This course focuses on leadership which includes individual and group communication, project planning, strategy, and individual development, with a focus on Information Technology and its uses. Projects focus on exposing, engaging, and recruiting women and minorities to the IT/computing field, promoting the IT/ICT major, community technology engagement, and K-12 tech initiatives.

title: Introduction to Networks and Telecommunications
description: A foundation course in networking technologies and management of modern data networks, with emphasis on the building blocks of local area networks. Subjects covered include networking architectures, topologies, models, layers, protocols, IP subnetting, equipment, operating systems, security and various tools/utilities.

title: Network Administration for the Information Professional
description: This course focuses on the planning, design, configuration, operation, and management of computer networks containing data communication devices, servers, workstations, and networked applications and support systems.

title: Information & Data Visualization
description: This course examines the theory and practice of data visualization, with a focus on using programming languages to create graphics. Students explore how visual representations shape perception, enhance communication, and support evidence-based inquiry.

title: IT Professions
description: This course is designed to assist graduating seniors to articulate what they have learned from their training through the preparation of an Interactive Resume and Career Portfolio. Class discussions and assignments will help students prepare for their chosen career path.

title: Data Mining and Analytics
description: This course provides an intro to data analytics, which uses statistical and quantitative analysis, predictive and exploratory models to drive decisions and actions from data. Students learn basic concepts and algorithms for data exploration, data cleaning, predictive modeling, clustering, and text mining.

title: Information Security
description: This course provides a comprehensive, integrated and up-to-date overview of computing security. Topics include cybersecurity overview, cryptographic tools, user authentication, access control, malicious software, denial-of-service attacks, intrusion detection, firewalls and intrusion prevention systems, and buffer overflow.

title: Advanced Health Informatics
description: This course introduces students to emerging technological solutions that can help improve healthcare delivery and healthcare decision-making. It builds upon and extends the foundations presented in the basic health informatics course.

title: Advanced Information Security
description: This course offers advanced knowledge and skillsets on cyberinfrastructure security and contemporary issues in cybersecurity. Students will form teams to build their cyber defense systems and perimeters (as blue teams), and then conduct penetration testing (as red teams) in simulated live networks.

title: Introduction to Health Informatics
description: The growth of healthcare in the economy has generated the need for skilled information professionals specifically knowledgeable about emerging technical solutions that can help improve healthcare delivery and health decision making.

title: Information Technology Project
description: This course provides students with a broad perspective of project management through an information technology project. Students develop IT project management skills, IT product development, and hands-on experience.

title: Advertising Strategy
description: This foundation course in advertising explores creativity in a workshop environment.

title: Principles of Advertising
description: This course explores advertising and promotion as related to level of economic growth, cultural influences, and sociolegal environments.

title: Mass Media Law
description: This course offers a comprehensive review of laws, rules, and regulations affecting both the advertising and broadcast industries as well as other forms of mass media. Topics include libel, slander, invasion of privacy, gathering of information, and copyright laws.

title: Hispanic Marketing Communication
description: This course prepares undergraduate students to become educated decision makers and consumers of information regarding U.S. Hispanic marketing communication issues.

title: Advertising Team I
description: This course is application-based and provides students with the opportunity to develop a complete Integrated Marketing Communication campaign plan as part of the National Student Advertising Competition sponsored by the American Advertising Federation.

title: Advertising Team II
description: This is the second of a two-course sequence focused on campaign execution, developing a complete Integrated Marketing Communication campaign plan as part of the National Student Advertising Competition.

title: Advertising Copywriting
description: This course is designed for advertising majors. The course explores different types of ad writing and allows students to work on exercises that reinforce styles, grammar, and conciseness.

title: Media Planning
description: This course explores the coordination of advertising and marketing research, planning, creative strategy, and selection of media and production activities leading to the development of advertising campaigns.

title: Multicultural Marketing Communication
description: This course is geared to train students to become effective communicators and marketers when reaching out to multicultural society.

title: Account Planning
description: This course teaches students how to become resourceful, creative, and strategic to represent the consumer's voice in planning a marketing communication campaign, emphasizing applied research in consumer insights building, brief creative writing, debriefing, and strategic planning.

title: Online Communication and Presence
description: This course provides students with theoretical background and practical experience in constructing messages for online communication, as well as managing self-presentation and professional relationships in the online environment.

title: Contemporary Issues in Communication
description: This course introduces contemporary issues in communication, including communication as an academic discipline, a major business and governmental policy sector, and a professional career.

title: Careers in Communication
description: This course is designed to help Media/Communication Studies students identify career goals, analyze career fields in communication, create a resume and cover letter, and demonstrate interviewing skills.

title: Communication for Business and the Professions
description: This workplace-oriented course provides practical education and experience in the performance of informative, persuasive, and special occasion speeches through individual and group presentations.

title: Communication Research Methods
description: This course is an introduction to communication research methods. It examines survey, experimental, observational, and content analysis methods, along with philosophy of science, research design, measurement, sampling, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and reporting.

title: New Communication Technology and Contemporary Society
description: This course relates the development and the use of new communication technologies to a variety of issues, such as social, economic, health, and policy implications.

title: Media Culture and the Environment
description: This course examines the role of language and representation in our understanding of the natural world, examining news media coverage of environmental issues, environmental images in popular culture, and communication strategies of environmental organizations.

title: Media Representation
description: This course explores, observes, discusses, and understands the functions and effects of the ways in which global media represents marginalized peoples and communities.

title: Queer Studies
description: This course reviews and explores the foundational concepts of queer theory and queer history.

title: Political Communication and Campaigning
description: This course explores campaigns, elections, and American politics in a communication framework, including planning campaign strategies.

title: Digital Media Campaigns
description: This course introduces important ethical issues in developing digital media campaigns as well as providing practical experience in writing, designing, and executing a digital media campaign strategy.

title: Desktop Multimedia
description: This course provides overview of operations and applications of software packages; principles of design and presentation for print-based as well as audio-visual productions.

title: Social Marketing
description: This course is an overview and application of social marketing principles and campaigns, designed to familiarize students with current theory and provide experience planning a social marketing campaign.

title: Social Media Campaigns
description: This course prepares students to design and implement a social media campaign, and introduces them to the social, political, and ethical contexts of using new technologies.

title: Writing to Persuade
description: This course teaches students how to identify and apply the persuasive techniques and strategies for writing in a way that influences audiences to think and act in certain ways.

title: Global and Intercultural Communication
description: This course introduces students to theories, processes, and practices of effective communication across cultures, underscoring ideas of global communication as inter-cultural communication.

title: Social Responsibility (Rhetorically Speaking)
description: This course acquaints students with the principles of communication and the role it plays in social justice movements.

title: Communication Matters - Personal Responsibility in Public Speaking
description: This course covers both the principles of and the practical experience of public speaking with an emphasis on personal responsibility.

title: Media Culture and the Environment
description: This course examines the role of language and representation in our understanding of the natural world, examining news media coverage of environmental issues and communication strategies of environmental organizations.

title: Introduction to the Mass Media
description: This course covers a historical and social overview of the mass media and their relationship to the mass communication process in a modern society.

title: Positive Media Psychology
description: This course focuses on the positive effects of media use and examines the ways that media can inspire audiences, affect positive emotions, influence prosocial attitudes and behaviors, and improve well-being.

title: Documentary Film History Theory and Practice
prerequisites: Admission to a major in the School of Communication
description: This course surveys major trends in the documentary film tradition from the early 20th century until today, exploring expository, experimental, aesthetic, and rhetorical documentary practices.

title: Media Sports and Society
description: This course introduces students to various aspects of the sports-media relationship, including the history, industries, audiences, and social issues that arise from the relationship.

title: Media Law and Digital Innovation
prerequisites: MMC 2000, admission to School of Communication major
description: This course reviews legal principles related to digital communication media, and law and policy questions encountered in innovation in media content production, distribution and use in online and new media platforms.

title: Media Ethics
description: This course surveys the ethical principles, standards, and problems in the practice of journalism, advertising, and/or public relations.

title: Diffusion of Innovations
description: This course is an analysis of the process of change, particularly from the standpoint of how communication is used in the introduction, spread, and adoption of new ideas, behaviors, and products within a society.

title: Comparative and International Media Studies
description: This course is an examination of various international and national media systems and the elements which determine the type of media currently operating throughout the world.

title: Writing Media Criticism
description: This course investigates media criticism with an emphasis on composition, focusing on dominant critical perspectives that contribute to our understanding of media and its role in society.

title: Mass Media and Society
description: This course is an analysis of the effects of mass media on public opinion and behavior, including a review of social science research exploring the impact of TV on children and others.

title: Political Economy of Media
description: This course covers the structure and functions of U.S. and other mass-communication systems as well as their relationship to the political and economic systems.

title: Digital Games
description: This course analyzes existing games as interactive entertainment media, covering history, effects, player characteristics, moral aspects, community, and application to a variety of contexts.

title: Performance Studies
description: This course allows students to collect, analyze, and perform personal narratives and everyday conversations.

title: Introduction to Public Relations
description: This course introduces the student to the principles and practices of the public relations profession throughout all organizations using public relations.

title: Public Relations Strategy
description: This course covers the tools and techniques of public relations. Students learn the application of public relations principles.

title: Writing for Public Relations
description: This course is designed to develop professional-level writing skills for public relations.

title: Crisis Communication
description: This course is an advanced undergraduate seminar focusing on the theoretical analysis, practical strategies, and assessments of implications for all publics of national and international crisis communication situations.

title: Public Relations Campaigns
description: This is the capstone course for all undergraduate public relations students, focusing on the design and implementation of a public relations campaign using original research, integrated strategies, a comprehensive campaign plan, and detailed collateral material.

title: Media Techniques
description: This course introduces students to basic principles and terminology associated with the aesthetics of film making and television production.

title: Writing for the Electronic Media
description: This course teaches non-fiction writing for recently evolved electronic media, fostering an understanding of writing for television, radio, social media, blogs, podcasts, vlogs, webisodes, and other forms of electronic media.

title: Single-Camera Video Production
description: This course addresses direction and production of single-camera video projects including camera, audio, lighting, and linear editing.

title: Multiple Camera Studio Production
prerequisites: Admission to Digital Media Production major
description: This course is a professional experience course designed to give students experience operating various roles in a multi-camera production environment.

title: Digital Media Production Workshop
description: This course consists of advanced editing and postproduction techniques applied to field and studio projects, with emphasis on digital non-linear editing systems.

title: Television Interviewing and Hosting
description: This course introduces students to on-camera interviewing and hosting of news and public affairs programs including research and writing components.

title: Computer Graphics and Animation
description: This course studies the design and production of computer-generated graphics and animation for video projects.

title: 3D Video Animation
description: This course covers the techniques used to prepare, create, and post-produce 3D graphics and animation with video.

title: Video Workshop
description: This course is designed for students to gain experience in the production of television programs and video projects.

title: Radio Practicum
description: This course consists of radio work and day-to-day broadcast operations with an emphasis on practical application in management or advanced roles at the student radio station.

title: Advocacy Video Theory and Practice
prerequisites: RTV 3531, RTV 3571, admission to Media Production major
description: This course explores the theory and practice of short-form video production and examines social media distribution possibilities for these videos.

title: Documentary Video Production
description: This course offers instruction in the theory and practice of production of non-fiction documentary video, producing a final video product after studying the documentary tradition, theory, and history.

title: Immersive Documentary Production
prerequisites: Admission to Digital Media Production major
description: This course explores the ways that immersive media is being used to tell reality-based stories, developing working prototypes of immersive documentaries.

title: Television Practicum
description: This course consists of producing and directing television programs and video projects.

title: Advanced Post-Production
prerequisites: Admission to Digital Media Production major
description: This course is a hands-on introduction to editing for digital video, covering compression and codecs, video editing, basic motion graphics, color correction, audio editing, and exporting.

title: Advanced Lighting and Cinematography
description: This course focuses on advanced lighting and cinematography theory, techniques, and aesthetics, with students producing original content over the semester.

title: Immersive Video Production
prerequisites: RTV 3531, RTV 3571, admission to DMP major
description: This course explores new camera technology and software for post-production of immersive media, identifying best practices for producing, shooting, editing and displaying immersive video products.

title: Advanced Feature Production
description: This course gives students professional production experience acting as production crew on program features, including videography, editing, audio, and graphic design.

title: Advanced Feature Reporting
description: This course gives students scriptwriting, producing, voiceover and on-camera experience while promoting FSU through creative and informative visual storytelling.

title: Broadcast Operations and Management
description: This course explores the purpose, function, organization, and management of broadcast operations with an emphasis on advanced application, understanding, and skills-building.

title: Fundamentals of Speech
description: This course provides a survey and application of communication theory, including interpersonal communication, small group communication, and public speaking.

title: Public Speaking
description: This course covers the principles of and the practical experience of public speaking. The course is required of all majors.

title: Global Perspectives Communication
description: This course gives students an introduction to the basic processes of intercultural communication from a global perspective.

title: Contemporary Human Communication
description: This introductory course surveys current scholarship in five areas of communication theory: group, rhetorical, interpersonal, legal, and performance communication.

title: Classical Rhetoric
description: This course allows students to examine the origins of rhetorical theory during the classical period, emphasizing ideas on rhetoric of Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, and Quintillian.

title: Interpersonal Communication
description: This course is a survey of recent literature on interpersonal communication including such topics as self-concept, emotional behavior, interpersonal conflict, and interpersonal attraction.

title: Nonverbal Communication
description: This course is a review of recent literature on nonverbal communication including such topics as kinesics, proxemics, kinesthetic behavior, environment, physical characteristics, and personal appearance.

title: Art and Entertainment The Hidden Persuaders
description: This course is an analysis of drama as an instrument for advancing a political or social thesis.

title: Persuasion
description: This course is a study of the psychology of attitude formation and change, covering theories of persuasion and principles of persuasive communication across multiple contexts.

title: The Principles of Speechwriting
description: This course explores the history and principles of speechwriting, the ethical issues involved, and speechwriting skills based on sound principles of communication.

title: Methods of Rhetorical Criticism
description: This course examines methods for the practice of doing criticism of rhetorical discourse, covering Aristotelian, Metaphor, narrative, post-modern, and cultural approaches to the analysis of texts.

title: Interracial Intercultural Communication
description: This course helps students gain knowledge of the theory and process of interracial and intercultural communication.

title: Gender and Communication
description: This course is designed to help students gain knowledge of the theory and process of gender communication (about and between genders) from an interpersonal context perspective.
